trades.holding_period_note: sessions_held is measured per closed tranche of an average-cost lot, so tranches of the same lot share its entry date and their intervals overlap; they must not be summed. sessions_in_market is the union.

costs.note_price_difference: slippage_bps / price_difference is measured against the decision mid and therefore INCLUDES intraday drift (it can be negative). execution_cost_bps is friction only.

implementation_shortfall.note: drift is the mid's own movement between decision and execution; it is a timing outcome, not a fee, and is reported separately from the friction components.

pnl_decomposition.note: Realized and open P&L are net of explicit cash costs (commission, exchange and regulatory fees less rebates), which are the only costs charged to cash separately; spread, depth and impact are already inside the fill prices. The residual is the rounding gap and is reported rather than hidden.

narrative.verdict: made money but lagged the index
narrative.headline: Made money but lagged the index: +1.65% total return vs +14.41% for the index, -22.90pp residual after beta, -26.6% max drawdown, 0.40% of capital lost to execution costs.

clauses.text: Finished at +1.65%, profitable but 12.77pp behind the S&P 500's +14.41%.
The momentum premium went against the declared exposure (-5.87% for a +0.5 loading) yet the account still returned +1.65% - the result was driven by something other than this factor.
The beta premium this participant is built to harvest was live (+24.72% over the season) and the account made money - a tailwind that cannot be separated from skill on one path.
The reversal premium this participant is built to harvest was live (-11.49% over the season) and the account made money - a tailwind that cannot be separated from skill on one path.
Of the +1.65% total, about +24.55pp is explained by carrying beta 1.70 against a +14.41% market (R^2 0.34); the residual -22.90pp is everything else - selection, timing, leverage and cost.
CVNA contributed +6,753 USD (409% of net P&L) across 22 closed trades; MSFT was the biggest drag at -5,709 USD.
Execution cost 396 USD (0.40% of starting capital, 0.5 bp per fill, 0.6 bp of the 6,809,474 USD traded). 70% of that was spread/depth/impact and 30% was explicit fees and rebates.
335 closed round trips, 66.9% winners, profit factor 1.01, average winner +285 vs average loser -570 USD, median holding 19 sessions.

Worst peak-to-trough drawdown -26.57% (-9.10% for the index), trough on 2026-03-30, recovered 2026-06-18. Average gross exposure 137% of starting capital, peak leverage 2.08x.
Daily returns were +0.19 skewed with excess kurtosis +4.99; historical 95% VaR -3.62%/day with CVaR -5.28%/day. Worst single session -11.74%, best +10.67%.

The style premia quoted above are measured on the simulated replay, whose cross-sectional drifts are DECLARED scenario parameters (see sim/universe.py). They describe this competition, not the real market: IR-16.
Declared failure mode(s) that actually fired: The regime filter is a lagging index average, so the book goes to cash after the drop, not before.

Declared failure mode(s) this run CANNOT test, because no measurable condition matches their wording (they are neither confirmed nor ruled out): Stacking correlated signals is not diversification: they all fail on the same days.
Season context: the real S&P 500 fell 9.10% from 2026-01-27 to 2026-03-30, VIX peaked at 31.05 on 2026-03-27, and cross-sectional dispersion was 61.5pp (stdev of individual 1-year returns).

prose.title: Mandate (as declared before the season)
prose.text: @KitchenSink_AllIn (Kitchen Sink) ran the "signal stacking" archetype. Declared thesis: Stack the signals instead of choosing between them. A name that is simultaneously above its 50-session EMA, inside 5% of its 63-session high, positive on 21-session momentum and in a rising-market regime gets the full 2x allocation. Names that fail any test get nothing. Entry: EMA20 > EMA50 on prior closes; Close within 5% of the 63-session high; 21-session momentum > 0; Index above its 50-session mean (regime filter); Equal weight across all qualifying names, scaled to 2.0x gross. Exit: A name is dropped the moment it fails any test; The whole book goes to cash if the regime filter fails. Sizing: 2.0x gross divided equally across qualifying names. Leverage: 2.0x gross or 0x. Cadence: daily, horizon days to weeks. Aggression 4/5. This participant was built to maximise return, not to manage risk: Refuses to hold anything that is not confirming on every axis, then sizes the survivors to the cap.
